The search did not turn up a clear arXiv 2026 paper on RAG evaluation. The results were mostly older survey and benchmark papers, a 2026 conference paper, and vendor blog posts.

- **Survey (arXiv-style, undated here):** A survey titled "Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey" proposes a unified evaluation process called Auepora and reviews existing RAG benchmarks against it. It groups metrics into retrieval metrics and generation metrics, and covers LLM-as-a-judge scoring.
- **LIT-RAGBench (2026):** This is a benchmark paper in the LREC 2026 proceedings, not arXiv. It targets the generator side of RAG and argues that existing benchmarks for Generators provide limited coverage, with none enabling simultaneous evaluation of multiple capabilities under unified conditions.
- **RGB (AAAI 2024):** This is an older but widely cited benchmark. It tests noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness in English and Chinese, and the authors found that LLMs still struggle significantly in terms of negative rejection, information integration, and dealing with false information.
- **Vendor blog (low confidence):** A getwidget.dev page describes a "2026-Q2" RAG benchmark that scores recall, faithfulness, and cost across model families. It is a commercial page with no peer review, and its results were still listed as targeted for June 2026, so I would not rely on its numbers.

If you need arXiv specifically, a follow-up search on arxiv.org with terms like "RAG evaluation" and "2026" would be the next step.

Links: [{"title":"Deepchecks: Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2605.14488v1"},{"title":"RAG Playground: A Framework for Systematic Evaluation of Retrieval Strategies and Prompt Engineering in RAG Systems","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2412.12322v1"},{"title":"[2504.07803] A System for Comprehensive Assessment of RAG Frameworks","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07803"},{"title":"RagChecker: A Fine-grained Framework for Diagnosing Retrieval-Augmented Generation","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2408.08067v2"},{"title":"[2408.01262] RAGEval: Scenario Specific RAG Evaluation Dataset Generation Framework","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.01262"},{"title":"RAGChecker: A Fine-grained Framework for Diagnosing Retrieval-Augmented Generation","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.08067"},{"title":"A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Academic Literature Navigation in Data Science","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2412.15404"},{"title":"[2309.15217] Ragas: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15217"},{"title":"[2410.12248] CoFE-RAG: A Comprehensive Full-chain Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Enhanced Data Diversity","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.12248"},{"title":"EncouRAGe: Evaluating RAG Local, Fast, and Reliable","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2511.04696v1"}]

The most-cited option is **Ragas**, which introduces a framework for reference-free evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines. Other RAG evaluation papers from the search:

- **RAGChecker** (arXiv 2408.08067) offers diagnostic metrics for both retriever and generator, and reports better correlations with human judgments than other evaluation metrics in meta-evaluation.
- **CoFE-RAG** (arXiv 2410.12248) covers the whole pipeline, including chunking, retrieval, reranking, and generation, and also releases a benchmark dataset.
- **RAGEval** (arXiv 2408.01262) is a dataset-generation framework for specialized scenarios, and its LLM-based scoring is consistent with human evaluations.
- **SCARF** (arXiv 2504.07803) is a black-box framework for benchmarking deployed RAG applications, including across vector databases and LLM serving setups.
- **RAG Playground** (arXiv 2412.12322) compares retrieval strategies and prompt engineering, combining programmatic, LLM-based, and hybrid metrics.
- **Deepchecks** (arXiv 2605.14488) is a newer paper that pairs root cause analysis with production monitoring.

For a general starting point, Ragas or RAGChecker are the most established. The results don't say which one fits a particular use case, so check each paper's scope against your needs.

content.text:
Here are three papers on evaluating RAG systems. I only have search-result snippets for them, not the full texts.

1. **Deepchecks: Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)** (arXiv 2605.14488, May 2026). This is the most recent of the three. It pairs root-cause analysis with production monitoring. [arxiv.org/html/2605.14488v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.14488v1)

2. **CoFE-RAG: A Comprehensive Full-chain Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation** (arXiv 2410.12248, Oct 2024). It evaluates the whole pipeline: chunking, retrieval, reranking and generation. It also releases a benchmark dataset with more diverse data. [arxiv.org/abs/2410.12248](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.12248)

3. **RAGChecker: A Fine-grained Framework for Diagnosing Retrieval-Augmented Generation** (arXiv 2408.08067, Aug 2024). It offers diagnostic metrics for both the retriever and the generator. Its authors report better correlation with human judgments than other evaluation metrics. [arxiv.org/abs/2408.08067](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.08067)

Only the Deepchecks paper is from 2026. If you need more 2026 work, two more candidates came up:

- **LIT-RAGBench**, from the LREC 2026 proceedings, is a benchmark for the generator side of RAG. I didn't find its link, so I can't point you to it.
- **SCARF** (arXiv 2504.07803, Apr 2025) is a black-box framework for benchmarking deployed RAG applications. [arxiv.org/abs/2504.07803](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07803)

- [RAGChecker](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.08067)
- [SCARF](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07803)
